gate: No third-party users before Phase 7 (GDPR). Phases 1-6 run on owner's own CV data only.
models: Free tiers only (cheap|smart) until Phase 8 benchmark. premium is BLOCKED.

0.what: BPCP workflow executor (instances, wait-for-signal, row locking)

1.what: Scaffold, auth guard, master CV import, MD/fact graph, drift detector

2.what: JD ingest (SSRF-guarded fetcher, paste fallback), requirement parser, fit scorer with citation validation

3.what: Tailoring (constrained generation) + entailment validator + ai-tell + word-level diff + eval harness

4.what: Voice revision loop, approve, PDF/DOCX export

6.what: Cover letters, screening answers, proof-of-work surfacing

7.what: GDPR: pseudonymization, consent, delete-cascade, export, retention

8.what: Model benchmark across tiers; gates premium and all pricing

9.what: Premium enablement, only if Phase 8 justifies it

tests.note: 11 skipped are integration tests needing a live Postgres; a higher skip count means a regression

Phase 3 eval harness has no recorded baseline yet: run src/applications/__evals__/run-eval.ts against a live ai-microservice and record the table before the next prompt edit. The 2026-08-23 blocker (ai-microservice returning model_used: "smart", a tier name, which cv-tuning correctly flagged as degraded) was FIXED on 2026-08-24 via resolution (a): ai-microservice now reports the real upstream model id and adds tier_used + model_resolved to the /ai/complete contract, so a tier name can no longer pose as a model id. cv-tuning treats model_resolved=false as degraded outright. NOT YET VERIFIED against the deployed ai-microservice: the fix is committed but the eval has not been re-run, so the baseline is still unrecorded and the deployed behaviour is unconfirmed.

Phase 4 export produces a name + ONE honest section ("Tailored Highlights"), not a full multi-section CV. Full reconstruction with real per-entry org/period needs a schema change: facts must carry section/org/period explicitly, or the master CV must be parsed structurally at import. Top Phase 5 candidate.
No retry path after an export failure at approve: the application sits `approved` with `stateError` and cannot be re-approved (the state guard rejects non-in_review). Phase 5 candidate.
Bullet identity is text-string equality only — TailoredBullet has no stable id, so two overreach bullets with identical text in one render are indistinguishable to confirmClaim and the approval gate.
traps: db-server-postgres Service has no selector: kubectl port-forward svc/... fails. Use kubectl exec into the cv-tuning pod.
git merge does not trigger auto-deploy (post-commit hook only, no post-merge). Batch branches need enqueue.sh or ./scripts/deploy.sh.
AI client timeout must stay above LiteLLM proxy 120s or the fallback chain never runs.
Probe a pod from inside itself via its podIP, not localhost — the app does not bind loopback.
No standalone TypeORM data-source: migrations run via migrationsRun at boot. Scratch-DB checks need a direct DataSource script.

pdf-parse's bundled pdf.js throws inside Jest's node environment for ANY PDF (verified with a bare jest config, no ts-jest or Nest involved). Production is unaffected. cv-pdf.service.spec.ts shells out to a child node process to assert extracted text — anyone calling pdf-parse live under Jest will hit this.

pdfkit's built-in Helvetica is WinAnsi-only: CJK, emoji, and Arabic silently corrupt in PDF output. CvPdfService now RAISES on unencodable characters, naming them and pointing at DOCX (which renders them correctly). Real Unicode font support is deferred — needs an embedded TTF, a licence decision, and a Docker image change.

pdfkit hashes info.CreationDate into the PDF /ID trailer, so an unpinned CreationDate makes the sha256 wall-clock dependent. It is pinned to new Date(0) because spec §6.3 reuses that sha256 for artifact idempotency.
